scenes.tts: A cochlear implant gives many adults with severe hearing loss useful hearing. The same idea in the eye often gives streaks, not pixels. Why?
scenes.visual: Split screen: an implant user listening on the left, a retina with a bright streak on the right. Question on screen: why the difference?
scenes.narration: A cochlear implant gives many adults with severe hearing loss useful hearing. The same idea in the eye often gives streaks, not pixels. Why?

scenes.tts: The implant skips damaged hair cells and excites the auditory nerve along the cochlea's map. High frequencies go to the base, low toward the apex.
scenes.visual: An unrolled cochlea drawn as a frequency ruler: high at the base, low at the apex. An electrode array slides in; current pulses jump from the contacts to a row of auditory-nerve neurons.
scenes.narration: The implant skips damaged hair cells and excites the auditory nerve along the cochlea's map. High frequencies go to the base, low toward the apex.

scenes.tts: A contact is hardware on the array. A channel is a band of frequencies. Truly separate channels need separate groups of neurons.
scenes.visual: Three labelled cards: contact (a gold dot), channel (a frequency band), neural group (a cluster of neurons under each channel).
scenes.narration: A contact is hardware on the array. A channel is a band of frequencies. Truly separate channels need separate groups of neurons.

scenes.tts: Predict. Take twenty-two contacts, spanning about sixteen millimetres. Each contact's current spreads through fluid and bone. How many non-overlapping stretches fit along the array?
scenes.caption: Predict. Take 22 contacts, spanning about 16 mm. Each contact's current spreads through fluid and bone. How many non-overlapping stretches fit along the array?
scenes.visual: 22 gold contacts light up one by one. On screen: 22 contacts, 0.75 mm apart, span about 16 mm; spread per contact about 1.75 mm (illustrative). Counter: non-overlapping stretches = ?
scenes.narration: Predict. Take 22 contacts, spanning about 16 mm. Each contact's current spreads through fluid and bone. How many non-overlapping stretches fit along the array?

scenes.tts: About nine, far fewer than twenty-two. Neighbouring fields overlap and excite the same neurons. This is called channel interaction.
scenes.caption: About nine, far fewer than 22. Neighbouring fields overlap and excite the same neurons. This is called channel interaction.
scenes.visual: Each contact's excitation drawn as a soft cloud on the nerve, fading at its edges; the clouds overlap. On screen: 16 mm / 1.75 mm = about 9. Label: toy 1-D packing exercise, about 9 non-overlapping stretches; not a measured or predicted channel count. Second label: channel interaction.
scenes.narration: About nine, far fewer than 22. Neighbouring fields overlap and excite the same neurons. This is called channel interaction.

scenes.tts: The spread was picked to land near real data, so this illustrates the idea rather than testing it. In eighteen implant users, speech recognition plateaued at eight to ten channels.
scenes.caption: The spread was picked to land near real data, so this illustrates the idea rather than testing it. In 18 implant users, speech recognition plateaued at 8 to 10 channels.
scenes.visual: A tag on 1.75 mm: illustrative, chosen to fit. A curve of speech score against the number of channels switched on rises, then flattens between 8 and 10. Label: Berg and colleagues, 2020; 18 adults.
scenes.narration: The spread was picked to land near real data, so this illustrates the idea rather than testing it. In 18 implant users, speech recognition plateaued at 8 to 10 channels.

scenes.tts: Channel interaction is one main reason. Neural survival and how far the array reaches matter too.
scenes.visual: Small icons beside the plateau: surviving neurons, insertion depth.
scenes.narration: Channel interaction is one main reason. Neural survival and how far the array reaches matter too.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. A prosthesis delivers detail only as far as it drives distinct groups of neurons.
scenes.visual: Callout box: the one idea. First line: detail only as far as it drives distinct groups of neurons, each in its place on the map.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. A prosthesis delivers detail only as far as it drives distinct groups of neurons.

scenes.tts: So a count of contacts is not a count of channels. That has to be measured, by testing what the listener can tell apart.
scenes.visual: Second line: contacts are not channels; measure what the listener can tell apart. Scope tag: spatial detail only, not a formula.
scenes.narration: So a count of contacts is not a count of channels. That has to be measured, by testing what the listener can tell apart.

scenes.tts: Test it. Some arrays are precurved, shaped to hug the inner wall, close to the nerve cell bodies in the cochlea's core.
scenes.visual: Cross-section of the cochlea: a straight array along the outer wall, and a precurved array hugging the inner wall near the spiral ganglion cell bodies in the modiolus.
scenes.narration: Test it. Some arrays are precurved, shaped to hug the inner wall, close to the nerve cell bodies in the cochlea's core.

scenes.tts: Predict. If spread sets the limit, what should a well-placed precurved array allow?
scenes.visual: The precurved array in the lower chamber, scala tympani. A blank channel curve waiting to be drawn.
scenes.narration: Predict. If spread sets the limit, what should a well-placed precurved array allow?

scenes.tts: More usable channels. In an earlier cohort from the same group, those listeners kept improving past ten.
scenes.caption: More usable channels. In an earlier cohort from the same group, those listeners kept improving past 10.
scenes.visual: A second curve keeps rising beyond 8 to 10 channels. Label: Berg and colleagues, 2019; precurved arrays well placed in scala tympani.
scenes.narration: More usable channels. In an earlier cohort from the same group, those listeners kept improving past 10.

scenes.tts: The plateau group had straight arrays, or precurved arrays that crossed into the upper chamber. Those generally sat farther from the nerve.
scenes.visual: The plateau curve returns, labelled: straight arrays, or translocated precurved arrays (crossed into scala vestibuli); generally farther from the modiolus. Tag: proposed explanation, more channel interaction.
scenes.narration: The plateau group had straight arrays, or precurved arrays that crossed into the upper chamber. Those generally sat farther from the nerve.

scenes.tts: So there is no single channel number. It depends on the listener, the placement and the test.
scenes.visual: Text on screen: no single channel number; listener, placement, test.
scenes.narration: So there is no single channel number. It depends on the listener, the placement and the test.

scenes.tts: None of this means the implant works poorly. In ninety-six adults, word scores rose by forty and a half percentage points. That was with the implant plus a hearing aid in the other ear.
scenes.caption: None of this means the implant works poorly. In 96 adults, word scores rose by 40.5 percentage points. That was with the implant plus a hearing aid in the other ear.
scenes.visual: A bar rising by 40.5 percentage points. Label: CNC words, 96 adults, six months, implant plus a hearing aid in the other ear; Buchman and colleagues, 2020.
scenes.narration: None of this means the implant works poorly. In 96 adults, word scores rose by 40.5 percentage points. That was with the implant plus a hearing aid in the other ear.

scenes.tts: So ask how distinctly a device drives separate groups of neurons, and test what the listener can tell apart.
scenes.visual: End line on screen: contacts are not channels; ask how distinctly the device drives separate groups, and test what the listener can tell apart.
scenes.narration: So ask how distinctly a device drives separate groups of neurons, and test what the listener can tell apart.
